findings.issue_text: In UsernamePasswordForm.java's challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String) override, the guard was inverted from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires user != null; on fresh-login failed attempts (badPasswordHandler and unknown-username paths) context.getUser() is still null, so fillContextForm() is no longer invoked for the re-rendered error page, causing error pages in passkeys-enabled realms to lose WebAuthn data (no hidden #webauthn form, no challenge, no 'username webauthn' autocomplete) so the browser's passkey autofill disappears exactly when the user is most likely to want it. Fix: gate on `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (user-agnostic) in challenge(context, error, field), matching UsernameForm's behavior.

In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the 'webauthn absent' assertion block is defective: `assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue())` can never succeed (if findElement returns an element the matcher throws AssertionError immediately, making the subsequent fail(...) line unreachable dead code), and `catch (Exception)` swallows any exception rather than just the expected NoSuchElementException, so driver/page errors (stale element, page not loaded, XPath/JS failure) are silently interpreted as 'webauthn button absent' and the test can false-pass without verifying the re-auth page state; it should use the narrow form `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as the sibling PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest already does.

In `UsernamePasswordForm.java`, the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` gate requires `user != null`, inverting the previous condition: `fillContextForm()` used to be invoked when `context.getUser() == null` (the first-login/username-not-yet-known case, in `authenticate()` and via the explicit null check in `challenge()`), but is now invoked only when the user is already set. As a result, first-time logins on realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm page (the default browser flow) render with no WebAuthn data at all — no challenge in the auth session, no `autocomplete="username webauthn"` on the username input, and no `webauth` form/conditional-mediation script — breaking passkey autofill on the initial login page, with error re-renders via `challenge(context, error, field)` similarly affected since they also gate on `user != null`. Users who have only a passkey (no password credential) are effectively locked out on first login because the page no longer offers any credential they can present, and the PR's own tests (`PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey`, `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, and `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`) contradict the new gating and would fail — the code and the tests cannot both be right. The fix is to fill the form whenever passkeys are enabled by dropping the `user != null` term (matching the no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` used in `UsernameForm`).

UsernameForm.java:47 — the changed condition `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` removes the `context.success()` fast-path during re-authentication whenever the realm policy enables passkeys, so the username form is always rendered and the flow stalls until an extra browser submission (or passkey pick) advances it; the gate checks only realm-level `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` with no per-user check that the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey credential, silently adding a full FreeMarker page render plus one HTTP round trip to every user's re-auth (including passkey-less users who gain nothing), a latency regression on the frequently executed re-authentication path (prompt=login, admin-console step-up, max_age)

UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 and :137 — the fill condition was inverted so fillContextForm now runs only for identified users (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null), meaning initial-login pages and error pages rendered during initial login (bad username/password) no longer receive the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, conditional-UI attributes, or autocomplete="username webauthn" markup from this authenticator; realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm execution without an extra WebAuthn flow execution will lose the passkey option on the initial login page after upgrade — a regression of a previously working flow with no migration note

WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-66 — shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false unconditionally, bypassing the empty-authenticators guard at WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-106, so identified users who have no passkey credentials now get a rendered passkey button/option that cannot succeed (page advertises an authentication method the user doesn't have)

UsernameForm.java:47 — re-authenticating users in passkey-enabled realms no longer auto-skip the username form (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()), so passkey-less users get an extra username page mid-re-auth with no USERNAME_HIDDEN handling, adding friction for users Keycloak already knows

Condition inversion regression in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) (lines 137-140) with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (lines 160-162): the old code filled webauthn form data exactly when context.getUser() == null, but the new code fills only when context.getUser() != null, so error re-renders for unidentified users (unknown/invalid username or missing username, where the user is still null) never call fillContextForm and the re-rendered login page has no webauthn challenge/rpId data. In a passkeys-enabled realm, a user who typos their username gets an error page where the passkey option has vanished (no webauth form, no username webauthn autocomplete, no conditional mediation), and passwordless-only users have no fallback except manually reloading. The gating should fill whenever passkeys are enabled (both identified and unidentified states), and this path is untested because the new/updated tests only exercise the valid-username error path (user != null).

Realm-level passkeys gating ignores whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey: the UsernameForm skip suppression (line 47) and UsernamePasswordForm webauthn setup (lines 113-115) are gated purely on the realm passkeys policy, never on the identified user's credentials, and because WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() (lines 64-66) now returns false, WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm no longer reaches the authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() early-return that previously suppressed the webauthn form for users with no webauthn credentials. As a result, password-only users in a passkeys-enabled realm suffer a per-re-auth friction regression: in UsernameForm-based flows they are no longer skipped past the username form and must retype their username into an empty visible input before reaching the re-authenticate password page, and in UsernamePasswordForm flows they are shown a passkey 'Authenticate' option that can never succeed for them. Checking the identified user's webauthn-passwordless credentials during re-auth would preserve the old flow, and the 'enabled policy, user without passkey' combination is untested (the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers passkeys disabled realm-wide).

Anonymous login through UsernamePasswordForm loses WebAuthn conditional-UI setup: the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gating (requires user != null) means the initial anonymous login page and the error page after a failed anonymous password attempt no longer receive WebAuthn data (the webauth form and autocomplete="username webauthn" disappear), contradicting the PR's own retained test assertions in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication — either these tests fail as submitted or the anonymous behavior silently regressed; a test is needed to pin the intended anonymous-page behavior (initial page and error page) for UsernamePasswordForm.

The new re-auth handling in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (the AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call at line 53 for the passkey-failure error page) is completely untested — no test triggers a failed WebAuthn assertion during re-auth; the new tests only cover failed password attempts, so if this call regresses or reads the wrong auth note, nothing catches it.

No test for manual username entry during re-auth in the UsernameForm flow: UsernameForm now renders the username form during re-auth instead of auto-succeeding, but no test types a username on the re-auth form — uncovered cases include (a) a user with password+passkey re-authenticating by typing username then password, and (b) the edge where a different username is submitted during re-auth, a newly reachable path with potential security implications if action() accepts a user other than the one being re-authenticated.

reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey doesn't test what its name claims: it disables passkeys at the realm-policy level (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), only covering the isPasskeysEnabled() == false branch; the case the name describes — passkeys policy enabled but the re-authenticating user has no passkey credential — is covered nowhere; rename the test or add the policy-enabled/user-without-passkey case.

Negative DOM assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey use a try/catch/fail anti-pattern that can false-pass: findElement never returns null (it throws NoSuchElementException), so assertThat(..., nullValue()) can never pass and the fail(...) is dead code; the broad catch (Exception) swallows any other exception (driver errors, page not loaded, stale element), so the 'webauthn button absent' check can pass for the wrong reason — use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead.

Missing test for re-auth with a non-discoverable/external key in the default UsernameForm flow: PasskeysUsernameFormTest only has external-key tests for fresh login, and its only re-auth test uses a discoverable key that auto-triggers conditional UI; external-key re-auth is only tested in UsernamePasswordForm-based flows — if the UsernameForm re-auth page offers no explicit WebAuthn entry point for non-discoverable keys, those users still cannot re-authenticate with their passkey after this fix.

Inverted dependency: `AuthenticatorUtils` (in the shared, lower-level util package) statically imports `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (browser package) at AuthenticatorUtils.java:35, while browser classes in the same PR call into `AuthenticatorUtils` (`badPasswordHandler`, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`), creating a bidirectional class/package dependency; the internal auth-note constant was widened from `protected` to `public` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58) solely to support it, making it de-facto public API. Move the constant into `AuthenticatorUtils` or a neutral constants class, have the browser class reference it from there, and revert the widening.
Helper method name `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` encodes its first caller's context and is already misleading at its second call site inside the WebAuthn authenticator.

Guard inversion in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` (~line 137): the predicate flipped from `context.getUser() == null && passkeysEnabled` (old) to `passkeysEnabled && user != null` (new), so on a fresh (non-re-auth) login with a wrong password — where `context.getUser()` is still null because invalid credentials never set the user — the re-rendered error page no longer gets `fillContextForm`, and the passkey option silently disappears after one mistyped password until reload; no test pins webauthn presence on the fresh-login error page (tests only assert it on the initial page and on re-auth pages where the user is set). If the passkey button should survive a failed attempt, the guard must cover the `user == null` case too.

Test antipattern in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (~lines 236 and 258): `try { assertThat(...); fail(...); } catch (Exception e) {}` makes the `fail()` unreachable dead code (if the element exists, `assertThat` throws `AssertionError`, which `catch (Exception)` does not catch), and the broad `catch (Exception)` swallows unrelated WebDriver failures (timeouts, stale elements) as 'element absent', producing false greens; use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` did before this PR removed it.

Duplicated auth-note parsing: the new util method in `AuthenticatorUtils.java` (~line 125) re-implements `Boolean.parseBoolean(context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))`, logic that already exists as `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`, whose only visible call site (`badPasswordHandler`) was removed — two independent readers of the same protocol note must be kept in sync (key renames or value-semantics changes must hit both), and the old method may now be dead code; consolidate on a single reader living next to the constant and delete the orphan.

Two same-named methods with different semantics: new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` in `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160` ('realm passkeys on AND user known') vs the existing no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` invoked at `UsernameForm.java:47` ('realm passkeys on'), each re-implementing `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` over separately constructed `webauthnAuth` instances in a parent/child class pair — same-name/different-semantics invites calling or editing the wrong one and lets the shared condition drift; reuse a single check or give the user-aware variant a distinct name.

Fill-guard `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context);` duplicated in both `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` (~line 113) and `challenge(error, field)` (~line 137), on top of passkeys-visibility decision points scattered across five sites in three classes (`UsernameForm.authenticate` skip, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`/`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, and the `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` override); there is no single place answering 'when is the passkeys UI shown', and the `authenticate` copy may double-execute `fillContextForm` via the inherited challenge path — centralize into one helper used by every render path.

Copy-pasted re-auth tests: `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` and `PasskeysUsernameFormFormTest`-style `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` share ~55 verbatim-identical lines, and `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` is a strict prefix of `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` in the same class — any change to the re-auth flow or event details requires synchronized edits in 3–4 places; extract the shared 'login with passkey, then re-auth with `prompt=login`' scaffolding into a helper and consider dropping the subsumed test.

Template-method hook with an undocumented invariant in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.java` (~lines 100 and 124): `fillContextForm`'s branch is gated on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but its body still dereferences the `user` local (`new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(..., user, ...)`); the base hook happens to return `context.getUser() != null`, so 'hook true implies user non-null' holds only implicitly and the javadoc does not state it — a future subclass returning `true` for a discoverable-credential scenario would NPE; document the contract or add a null-check so the hook is safe to override.
`isUserIdentified` flag name has drifted from its meaning — after the refactor it means 'show authenticator list' rather than 'user identified'; align the flag name with its post-refactor semantics.

The new passkeys gate in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162 (`webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`) inverts the old `user == null` condition, dropping conditional-UI setup on initial anonymous login: `fillContextForm` is never called on the first render of the username+password page, so the page never receives `challenge`, `rpId`, `userVerification`, or `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, and no `AUTH_CHALLENGE` auth note is stored — resulting in no `autocomplete="username webauthn"`, no conditional-mediation autofill, and no passkey form on initial login (also stripping the passkey option from error re-renders where the user couldn't be identified). The gate should keep covering `user == null` (i.e., effectively `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`), and as diffed the code contradicts its own test assertions (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey).

Removing the credential allow-list on newly-exposed identified-user pages opens an identity-substitution window: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63-65) returns `false` unconditionally, so `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` is never published even when a user is already identified, while the PR newly renders the passkey option on identified-user pages — so the browser is offered every discoverable credential for the RP, not just the identified user's. If `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.action` resolves the account from the assertion's `userHandle` without cross-checking the already-set context user, a visitor could type any organization member's username to pass the OrganizationAuthenticator membership check and then complete the org-scoped login with their own non-member passkey (org-membership bypass), and `prompt=login` re-auth could complete as a different identity than the one the client asked to re-verify. This case is untested; the action code must reject assertions whose `userHandle` doesn't match the identified context user.

The passkey option is now offered to identified users who have no passkey at all: with `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() == false`, the `authenticators.isEmpty()` early-return guard in `fillContextForm` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-106) is unreachable for the conditional-UI authenticator, and the new UsernamePasswordForm gate checks only the policy, not whether the identified user actually holds a passwordless credential — so during re-auth (or the org post-username page) users with no passwordless credential see a passkey button that dead-ends in a browser error and the `createErrorResponse` loop. Consider gating on `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS)`.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) from filling WebAuthn context when `context.getUser() == null` (and passkeys enabled) to only doing so when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null`. In this same PR, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator’s comment/doc indicates the user is normally cleared after unsuccessful password auth unless a special re-auth note is set (and the old inline re-auth setup was moved into AuthenticatorUtils). That makes it very plausible—and consistent with the previous `context.getUser()==null` guard—that after a failed password attempt the user is cleared, so the new guard prevents `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` from running when re-rendering the error page, dropping the WebAuthn/passkeys form setup on that error render.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the new “webauthn not available” checks are implemented as `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) {}` (done twice). `findElement` either returns a WebElement or throws (commonly NoSuchElementException); if it returns an element, `assertThat(element, nullValue())` throws AssertionError (an Error, not an Exception), so the `fail(...)` line is effectively dead/unreachable. More importantly, catching broad `Exception` will treat any runtime WebDriver/page issue (e.g., invalid selector, driver errors) as “expected”, allowing the test to false-pass without actually verifying absence. Using a narrow `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` (as other tests in the diff do) would avoid this masking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete behavior change in `UsernameForm.authenticate()`: the previous re-auth fast-path `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` is now gated by `&& !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, meaning when conditional passkeys are considered enabled the flow will no longer immediately `context.success()` for an already-identified user and will instead render the username step. That can add an extra rendered page / round-trip on the re-authentication path. However, the diff also adds multiple tests explicitly aiming to make passkeys work during re-authentication (prompt=login), suggesting this is an intentional tradeoff rather than a clear correctness defect. The finding’s additional claim that the gate is only realm-level and not per-user credential-based is not fully verifiable from the diff because `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 and :137 — the fill condition was inverted so fillContextForm now runs only for identified users (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null), meaning initial-login pages and error pages rendered during initial login (bad username/password) no longer receive the WebAuthn challenge, rpId, conditional-UI attributes, or autocomplete="username webauthn" markup from this authenticator; realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm execution without an extra WebAuthn flow execution will lose the passkey option on the initial login page after upgrade — a regression of a previously working flow with no migration note

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() and challenge(error,field), the code now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and isConditionalPasskeysEnabled explicitly requires user != null. That is a behavioral narrowing versus the prior logic (which did not require a non-null user at all, and per the removed comment was intended to run when the user was not already selected). From the diff alone, when context.getUser() is null (typical on initial login screen and often on error re-render before a user is established), the WebAuthn/passkeys form context will no longer be populated by UsernamePasswordForm, which can remove conditional-UI/passkey markup from pages in flows that rely on UsernamePasswordForm to provide it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-66 — shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false unconditionally, bypassing the empty-authenticators guard at WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-106, so identified users who have no passkey credentials now get a rendered passkey button/option that cannot succeed (page advertises an authentication method the user doesn't have)

adjudication.rationale: In WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(), the logic that instantiates WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean and handles the empty-authenticators case is now gated by shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) (changed from a direct user != null check). WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to return false unconditionally, so for this authenticator the empty-authenticators handling in fillContextForm() will never run even when context.getUser() is set. Given UsernamePasswordForm now calls fillContextForm when passkeys are enabled and user != null (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled), this change can result in conditional-passkey UI being prepared without checking whether the identified user actually has any WebAuthn credentials, potentially advertising an option that cannot succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 — re-authenticating users in passkey-enabled realms no longer auto-skip the username form (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()), so passkey-less users get an extra username page mid-re-auth with no USERNAME_HIDDEN handling, adding friction for users Keycloak already knows

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes UsernameForm.authenticate() from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, meaning re-authentication (where `context.getUser()` is already set) will no longer auto-skip the username step whenever conditional passkeys are considered enabled. The diff does not add any corresponding USERNAME_HIDDEN/registration-disabled handling for the UsernameForm itself (those attributes are only set in the new `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` and are invoked from password/passkey error paths), so the concern about added friction/extra screen in that scenario is grounded. However, whether this is definitively a “bug” depends on intended UX/flow semantics for conditional passkeys during re-authentication, which cannot be fully proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Condition inversion regression in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) (lines 137-140) with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (lines 160-162): the old code filled webauthn form data exactly when context.getUser() == null, but the new code fills only when context.getUser() != null, so error re-renders for unidentified users (unknown/invalid username or missing username, where the user is still null) never call fillContextForm and the re-rendered login page has no webauthn challenge/rpId data. In a passkeys-enabled realm, a user who typos their username gets an error page where the passkey option has vanished (no webauth form, no username webauthn autocomplete, no conditional mediation), and passwordless-only users have no fallback except manually reloading. The gating should fill whenever passkeys are enabled (both identified and unidentified states), and this path is untested because the new/updated tests only exercise the valid-username error path (user != null).

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field), the condition guarding webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) changed from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a real inversion: the old code populated WebAuthn/passkeys form context specifically when the user was *not* identified (user == null), but the new code only does so when the user *is* identified. Therefore, on error rerenders where the user remains null (e.g., missing/invalid username), the re-render path will no longer call `fillContextForm`, which can remove passkeys/webauthn form context from the error page. The added/updated tests in the diff focus on identified-user/re-authentication scenarios and do not cover the null-user error rerender case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Realm-level passkeys gating ignores whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey: the UsernameForm skip suppression (line 47) and UsernamePasswordForm webauthn setup (lines 113-115) are gated purely on the realm passkeys policy, never on the identified user's credentials, and because WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() (lines 64-66) now returns false, WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm no longer reaches the authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() early-return that previously suppressed the webauthn form for users with no webauthn credentials. As a result, password-only users in a passkeys-enabled realm suffer a per-re-auth friction regression: in UsernameForm-based flows they are no longer skipped past the username form and must retype their username into an empty visible input before reaching the re-authenticate password page, and in UsernamePasswordForm flows they are shown a passkey 'Authenticate' option that can never succeed for them. Checking the identified user's webauthn-passwordless credentials during re-auth would preserve the old flow, and the 'enabled policy, user without passkey' combination is untested (the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers passkeys disabled realm-wide).

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes passkeys UI/setup during re-authentication depend on realm-level passkeys enablement and the mere presence of an identified user, not on whether that user actually has any WebAuthn/passwordless credentials. Concretely, `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true for any non-null user when `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` is true, and then unconditionally calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` both in `authenticate()` and `challenge()`. Separately, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` now always returns false, so `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` will skip the block that instantiates `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and checks `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()`—removing the only visible credential-based suppression shown in this diff. This combination can cause passkey UI to be presented for a re-authenticating user who has no passkey credential, and `UsernameForm` also stops skipping when `context.getUser()!=null` if conditional passkeys are enabled, adding friction. The new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` explicitly sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it does not cover the problematic case (passkeys enabled, user has no passkey).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous login through UsernamePasswordForm loses WebAuthn conditional-UI setup: the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gating (requires user != null) means the initial anonymous login page and the error page after a failed anonymous password attempt no longer receive WebAuthn data (the webauth form and autocomplete="username webauthn" disappear), contradicting the PR's own retained test assertions in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication — either these tests fail as submitted or the anonymous behavior silently regressed; a test is needed to pin the intended anonymous-page behavior (initial page and error page) for UsernamePasswordForm.

The new re-auth handling in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (the AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call at line 53 for the passkey-failure error page) is completely untested — no test triggers a failed WebAuthn assertion during re-auth; the new tests only cover failed password attempts, so if this call regresses or reads the wrong auth note, nothing catches it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);` inside `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`, which only executes on the passkey-failure error path. The newly added/modified tests in this diff focus on re-authentication via `prompt=login`, successful WebAuthn logins, and failed password attempts during re-auth (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` checks an invalid password and that the WebAuthn form remains visible). None of the shown tests appears to simulate a *failed WebAuthn assertion* during re-authentication that would drive execution through `createErrorResponse`, so this new error-path behavior is not directly covered by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for manual username entry during re-auth in the UsernameForm flow: UsernameForm now renders the username form during re-auth instead of auto-succeeding, but no test types a username on the re-auth form — uncovered cases include (a) a user with password+passkey re-authenticating by typing username then password, and (b) the edge where a different username is submitted during re-auth, a newly reachable path with potential security implications if action() accepts a user other than the one being re-authenticated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to *not* auto-succeed when `context.getUser() != null` if conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). This makes a previously-skipped path reachable during re-authentication scenarios where the user is already set but passkeys are enabled (the username form is no longer skipped). The added tests cover re-auth with `prompt=login` largely via automatic passkey login or via the UsernamePasswordForm flow, but they do not exercise manual username entry on the re-auth username form nor the case of submitting a different username during re-auth in the UsernameForm flow. The security implication claim can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the missing test coverage for the newly reachable branch is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey doesn't test what its name claims: it disables passkeys at the realm-policy level (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), only covering the isPasskeysEnabled() == false branch; the case the name describes — passkeys policy enabled but the re-authenticating user has no passkey credential — is covered nowhere; rename the test or add the policy-enabled/user-without-passkey case.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, the new @Test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey sets realm policy `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and then asserts the WebAuthn form is absent during login and prompt=login re-auth. That only exercises the `isPasskeysEnabled() == false` path (passkeys disabled at realm level), not the scenario implied by the method name (passkeys enabled but the specific re-authenticating user has no passkey credential). The diff adds no test where passkeys are enabled and a user without a WebAuthn credential performs re-authentication, so the finding about misaligned test intent/coverage is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative DOM assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey use a try/catch/fail anti-pattern that can false-pass: findElement never returns null (it throws NoSuchElementException), so assertThat(..., nullValue()) can never pass and the fail(...) is dead code; the broad catch (Exception) swallows any other exception (driver errors, page not loaded, stale element), so the 'webauthn button absent' check can pass for the wrong reason — use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead.

Missing test for re-auth with a non-discoverable/external key in the default UsernameForm flow: PasskeysUsernameFormTest only has external-key tests for fresh login, and its only re-auth test uses a discoverable key that auto-triggers conditional UI; external-key re-auth is only tested in UsernamePasswordForm-based flows — if the UsernameForm re-auth page offers no explicit WebAuthn entry point for non-discoverable keys, those users still cannot re-authenticate with their passkey after this fix.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds re-authentication coverage for discoverable-key/passkeys in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` (`webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), but does not add any re-auth test for a non-discoverable/external key in the UsernameForm-based flow. The only expanded external-key re-authentication tests appear in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`). `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` still only has external-key coverage for fresh login (pre-existing `passwordLoginWithExternalKey`). This is a concrete test-gap tied to the newly adjusted re-auth/passkeys behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted dependency: `AuthenticatorUtils` (in the shared, lower-level util package) statically imports `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (browser package) at AuthenticatorUtils.java:35, while browser classes in the same PR call into `AuthenticatorUtils` (`badPasswordHandler`, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`), creating a bidirectional class/package dependency; the internal auth-note constant was widened from `protected` to `public` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58) solely to support it, making it de-facto public API. Move the constant into `AuthenticatorUtils` or a neutral constants class, have the browser class reference it from there, and revert the widening.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected` to `public` (services/.../AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java), and `AuthenticatorUtils` adds a `static import` of that constant (`import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`). At the same time, browser-layer classes now call into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (replacing inline logic in `badPasswordHandler`, and added in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). This creates an inverted/bidirectional dependency between a shared util package and browser authenticator classes, and the visibility widening is directly tied to enabling that access. This is a concrete architecture/API-surface concern grounded in the diff, not a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Helper method name `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` encodes its first caller's context and is already misleading at its second call site inside the WebAuthn authenticator.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the helper `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` is called from two places (password bad-credentials handler and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator#createErrorResponse`). The finding is essentially about the method name being misleading outside its original username/password error context. That is a naming/clarity concern (style/maintainability), not a verifiable behavior defect introduced by the diff, and doesn’t demonstrate an actual incorrect call/use from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guard inversion in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` (~line 137): the predicate flipped from `context.getUser() == null && passkeysEnabled` (old) to `passkeysEnabled && user != null` (new), so on a fresh (non-re-auth) login with a wrong password — where `context.getUser()` is still null because invalid credentials never set the user — the re-rendered error page no longer gets `fillContextForm`, and the passkey option silently disappears after one mistyped password until reload; no test pins webauthn presence on the fresh-login error page (tests only assert it on the initial page and on re-auth pages where the user is set). If the passkey button should survive a failed attempt, the guard must cover the `user == null` case too.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably flips the condition in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` from the old `context.getUser() == null && ...passkeysEnabled` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now requires `user != null`. This means the error re-render path will no longer call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in any case where the user is null at challenge time. Given Keycloak’s existing behavior of potentially clearing `context.getUser()` after bad password attempts (see the related re-auth handling refactor around `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`), this can regress conditional-passkeys UI persistence across a failed password attempt when the user ends up cleared, matching the finding’s described symptom. The added/modified tests mainly assert webauthn presence in flows where the user is already set (reauth / preselected user), not the user-null error rerender case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test antipattern in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (~lines 236 and 258): `try { assertThat(...); fail(...); } catch (Exception e) {}` makes the `fail()` unreachable dead code (if the element exists, `assertThat` throws `AssertionError`, which `catch (Exception)` does not catch), and the broad `catch (Exception)` swallows unrelated WebDriver failures (timeouts, stale elements) as 'element absent', producing false greens; use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` did before this PR removed it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` two blocks of `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}`. With Selenium `findElement`, the element is either returned (non-null) or a `NoSuchElementException` is thrown before the assertion. If the element exists, `assertThat(..., nullValue())` throws an `AssertionError` (not caught by `catch (Exception)`), so `fail()` is never reached; if the element does not exist, the exception is swallowed and the test passes. Additionally, `catch (Exception)` will also swallow unrelated WebDriver exceptions, potentially producing false-green tests. This is a real, diff-grounded defect in the test logic; using `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` (or `findElements().isEmpty()`) would avoid both issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated auth-note parsing: the new util method in `AuthenticatorUtils.java` (~line 125) re-implements `Boolean.parseBoolean(context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))`, logic that already exists as `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`, whose only visible call site (`badPasswordHandler`) was removed — two independent readers of the same protocol note must be kept in sync (key renames or value-semantics changes must hit both), and the old method may now be dead code; consolidate on a single reader living next to the constant and delete the orphan.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`, which directly parses the auth-note via `Boolean.parseBoolean(context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))` (new code in `AuthenticatorUtils.java`). In `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler`, the previous usage of `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` is removed and replaced by the new util call. The diff does not remove `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`, so within this PR there are now (at least) two independent implementations of the same auth-note interpretation (the existing helper method and the new util), creating a maintainability/sync risk and likely leaving the old helper potentially unused. This is not a behavior-breaking defect by itself, but it is a concrete consolidation/architecture issue grounded in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two same-named methods with different semantics: new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` in `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160` ('realm passkeys on AND user known') vs the existing no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` invoked at `UsernameForm.java:47` ('realm passkeys on'), each re-implementing `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` over separately constructed `webauthnAuth` instances in a parent/child class pair — same-name/different-semantics invites calling or editing the wrong one and lets the shared condition drift; reuse a single check or give the user-aware variant a distinct name.
matched_golden_ids: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that a new user-aware `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` exists, but `UsernameForm` still invokes the no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` at the relevant line, highlighting the mismatch/incorrect usage of the user-parameterized check. This aligns with the golden issue that the required `UserModel` parameter isn’t being passed in `UsernameForm.authenticate()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fill-guard `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context);` duplicated in both `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` (~line 113) and `challenge(error, field)` (~line 137), on top of passkeys-visibility decision points scattered across five sites in three classes (`UsernameForm.authenticate` skip, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`/`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, and the `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` override); there is no single place answering 'when is the passkeys UI shown', and the `authenticate` copy may double-execute `fillContextForm` via the inherited challenge path — centralize into one helper used by every render path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the same guard+call pattern in two render paths in `UsernamePasswordForm`: in `authenticate` it now unconditionally does `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`, and in `challenge(context, String error, String field)` it does the same check/call before delegating to `super.challenge(...)`. The visibility/decision logic is also split across multiple classes/methods added/changed here (`UsernameForm.authenticate` now avoids skipping the form when conditional passkeys are enabled; `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` now delegates to `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`; `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that to `false`). That fragmentation/duplication is a real maintainability/architecture concern introduced by this change. However, the claim that `authenticate` may “double-execute” `fillContextForm` via an inherited challenge path is not directly verifiable from the diff because we can’t see the implementation of `challenge(context, formData)` / superclass behavior, so it’s not a provable defect from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-pasted re-auth tests: `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` and `PasskeysUsernameFormFormTest`-style `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` share ~55 verbatim-identical lines, and `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` is a strict prefix of `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` in the same class — any change to the re-auth flow or event details requires synchronized edits in 3–4 places; extract the shared 'login with passkey, then re-auth with `prompt=login`' scaffolding into a helper and consider dropping the subsumed test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple new re-authentication tests with substantial duplicated scaffolding. In `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, the new `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` methods are visibly near-identical sequences (virtual authenticator setup, realm updater block, `registerDefaultUser()`, `logout()`, `oauth.openLoginForm()`, `events.expectLogin()`, then `prompt(OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN)` followed by another `events.expectLogin()` and `logout()`). In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`, the new `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` follows the same initial steps as the later `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` and is effectively a strict subset/prefix of that longer test (setup policy, register user, first WebAuthn login, `prompt=login`, second WebAuthn login, then the longer test continues with password-failure and reauth variants). This is a real maintenance/design concern grounded in the diff (not a runtime defect), and extracting shared helpers (and possibly dropping the subsumed test) would reduce synchronized edits when the flow/event assertions change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Template-method hook with an undocumented invariant in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.java` (~lines 100 and 124): `fillContextForm`'s branch is gated on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but its body still dereferences the `user` local (`new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(..., user, ...)`); the base hook happens to return `context.getUser() != null`, so 'hook true implies user non-null' holds only implicitly and the javadoc does not state it — a future subclass returning `true` for a discoverable-credential scenario would NPE; document the contract or add a null-check so the hook is safe to override.

adjudication.rationale: In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, the new guard `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))` wraps code that still dereferences the local `user` (`new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(..., user, ...)`). The default hook implementation currently returns `context.getUser() != null`, so it’s safe today, and the only shown override (`WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`) returns `false`. However, the new hook’s Javadoc does not state the required invariant (“if true, user must be non-null”), so a future subclass could return `true` when `context.getUser()` is null (e.g., a discoverable-credential flow) and trigger an NPE. This is a real, diff-grounded design/contract issue rather than an immediately verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isUserIdentified` flag name has drifted from its meaning — after the refactor it means 'show authenticator list' rather than 'user identified'; align the flag name with its post-refactor semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, the logic that previously keyed off `user != null` (i.e., “user identified”) is now gated by `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`. Since `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to always return `false`, the code path that sets/uses the local `isUserIdentified` flag can now be skipped even when `context.getUser() != null` (user is identified) purely to hide the authenticator list. That makes the name `isUserIdentified` potentially misleading post-refactor; aligning the flag name with “authenticator list shown” semantics would improve maintainability without being a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new passkeys gate in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162 (`webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`) inverts the old `user == null` condition, dropping conditional-UI setup on initial anonymous login: `fillContextForm` is never called on the first render of the username+password page, so the page never receives `challenge`, `rpId`, `userVerification`, or `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, and no `AUTH_CHALLENGE` auth note is stored — resulting in no `autocomplete="username webauthn"`, no conditional-mediation autofill, and no passkey form on initial login (also stripping the passkey option from error re-renders where the user couldn't be identified). The gate should keep covering `user == null` (i.e., effectively `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`), and as diffed the code contradicts its own test assertions (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey).
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: adding a `user != null` requirement prevents `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` (and thus conditional passkey UI setup) from running on the initial login page when `context.getUser()` is still null, breaking ID-less/conditional passkey login on first render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the credential allow-list on newly-exposed identified-user pages opens an identity-substitution window: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63-65) returns `false` unconditionally, so `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` is never published even when a user is already identified, while the PR newly renders the passkey option on identified-user pages — so the browser is offered every discoverable credential for the RP, not just the identified user's. If `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.action` resolves the account from the assertion's `userHandle` without cross-checking the already-set context user, a visitor could type any organization member's username to pass the OrganizationAuthenticator membership check and then complete the org-scoped login with their own non-member passkey (org-membership bypass), and `prompt=login` re-auth could complete as a different identity than the one the client asked to re-verify. This case is untested; the action code must reject assertions whose `userHandle` doesn't match the identified context user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a potentially risky inconsistency: UsernamePasswordForm now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when a user is already identified (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null), i.e., it newly enables conditional-passkey UI on identified-user pages. At the same time, WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(...) to always return false, which means WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(...) will skip building the per-user WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean when the user is identified. If that bean is what drives a per-user allow-list / UI-scoped authenticator restriction, this change could allow using a discoverable credential for a different account unless the action handler enforces userHandle == context.getUser(). However, the diff does not include the action/assertion verification code or any explicit ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS handling, so the claim that identity substitution is definitely possible cannot be verified from this diff alone; it remains a specific, diff-grounded security concern to double-check in action code/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The passkey option is now offered to identified users who have no passkey at all: with `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() == false`, the `authenticators.isEmpty()` early-return guard in `fillContextForm` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-106) is unreachable for the conditional-UI authenticator, and the new UsernamePasswordForm gate checks only the policy, not whether the identified user actually holds a passwordless credential — so during re-auth (or the org post-username page) users with no passwordless credential see a passkey button that dead-ends in a browser error and the `createErrorResponse` loop. Consider gating on `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS)`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes the conditional-UI authenticator skip the user-credential availability check in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()`: the `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` early-return is now inside `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to always return `false`, making that guard unreachable for conditional UI. At the same time, `UsernamePasswordForm` now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which only checks `webauthnAuth != null`, `isPasskeysEnabled()`, and `user != null`—not whether the identified user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential configured. From the diff alone, this combination can cause conditional passkeys UI setup to occur for identified users without any passkey credential, which is a likely broken UX/flow (offering a WebAuthn option that cannot succeed).
